effects: The signer sends exactly `assets` AUSD to the vault (safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets) in enter).
The vault mints fAUSDe shares to `onBehalf`. The number is previewDeposit(assets), set by the vault's share price, and the signer sets no minimum.
The vault first runs accrueInterest, which may mint fee shares to the fee recipients. This dilutes the price slightly but moves none of the signer's assets.
formats.shown: Deposit 5 AUSD for <onBehalf>, with the share ticker fAUSDe and the address that receives the shares; the number of shares is not shown.

findings.title: deposit does not show how many fAUSDe shares the signer receives; the vault price decides it
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. The calldata has no minimum-shares argument. Case 0: 5 fAUSDe went to the signer, and the screen shows only 'Share ticker: fAUSDe'.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds the share amount. Keep the 'Send shares to' field. A wallet could add a simulated share amount.

findings.title: deposit interpolatedIntent says 'for {onBehalf}' and does not name fAUSDe shares as what arrives
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit interpolatedIntent: "Deposit {#.assets} for {#.onBehalf}"; the separate raw field 'Share ticker' = $.metadata.constants.vaultTicker.
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to "Deposit {#.assets} for fAUSDe shares to {#.onBehalf}".

cases.notes: The screen states the 5 AUSD out and the vault correctly. The 5 fAUSDe in has the right asset and recipient, but its amount is not shown and cannot be.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns fAUSDe shares from `onBehalf`. The number is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up, and the calldata sets no maximum.
The vault sends exactly `assets` AUSD to `receiver`.
When msg.sender != onBehalf, the call spends the signer's share allowance from onBehalf by the number of shares burned.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly N AUSD to <receiver>, with an Owner field; the screen never says that fAUSDe shares are burned or how many.

findings.title: withdraw never says fAUSDe shares are burned from the owner; the label just says 'Owner'
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares);`. descriptor withdraw field onBehalf label "Owner"; interpolatedIntent "Withdraw {#.assets} to {#.receiver}". Case 2: 11.8426 fAUSDe left the signer, and the reader was unsure 'Whether receipt tokens or shares are given up'.
findings.fix: Rename the onBehalf label to "Burn fAUSDe shares from" and set interpolatedIntent to "Withdraw {#.assets} to {#.receiver} by burning fAUSDe shares".

findings.title: withdraw does not show the number of fAUSDe shares burned; the vault price decides it
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);`. The calldata has no maximum-shares argument. Case 2: 11842617072116611233 fAUSDe burned, and no amount is shown.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds it. A wallet could add a simulated share amount.

cases.notes: The 11.853428 AUSD in is exact and goes to the right recipient. The fAUSDe burned is not stated: the reader guessed it was a position but did not know the asset or the amount.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns exactly `shares` fAUSDe from `onBehalf`.
The vault sends previewRedeem(shares) AUSD to `receiver`. The vault price decides this amount, and the calldata sets no minimum.
When msg.sender != onBehalf, the call spends the signer's share allowance from onBehalf by `shares`.
formats.shown: Redeem N fAUSDe to <receiver>, with an Owner field; the screen never names AUSD as the asset received.

findings.title: redeem never names AUSD as the asset the receiver gets, though mint shows it as a constant
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);`. The redeem fields are only shares, receiver and onBehalf. Case 3: 199.987886 AUSD went to the signer, and the reader said 'The screen does not say which asset or how much.'
findings.fix: Add a field {"label": "Receive asset", "format": "raw", "value": "$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"}. Set interpolatedIntent to "Redeem {#.shares} for AUSD to {#.receiver}".

findings.title: redeem does not show how much AUSD is received; the vault price decides it, with no minimum
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);`. The calldata has no minimum-assets argument. Case 3: 199987886 AUSD in, and no amount is shown.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds it. A wallet could add a simulated output.

cases.notes: The 199.7579 fAUSDe out is exact. For the AUSD in, the screen shows only the recipient; the asset and the amount are missing.

effects: The signer sends previewMint(shares) AUSD to the vault, rounded up. The vault price decides the amount, and the calldata sets no maximum.
The vault mints exactly `shares` fAUSDe to `onBehalf`.
formats.shown: Mint N fAUSDe for <onBehalf>, with a 'Deposit asset: AUSD' field that has no amount.

findings.title: mint intent and sentence omit that the signer pays AUSD; only a ticker field hints at it
findings.evidence: descriptor mint intent "Mint" and interpolatedIntent "Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}"; field 'Deposit asset' = $.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker. VaultV2.sol enter: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets);`. Case 1: 1.000102 AUSD out.
findings.fix: Set intent to "Deposit AUSD for shares" and interpolatedIntent to "Pay AUSD to mint {#.shares} to {#.onBehalf}".

findings.title: mint does not show how much AUSD leaves the signer; the vault price decides it, with no cap
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. The calldata has no maximum-assets argument. Case 1: 1000102 AUSD out, and the screen shows only 'Deposit asset: AUSD'.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds it. A wallet could add a simulated cost.

cases.notes: AUSD out is named as the asset, but the amount (1.000102) is not shown and cannot be. The shares went to 0xdead, which the screen shows; that effect is not the signer's.
